canonical.title: Sum of Subarray Minimums
canonical.sourceFilePath: 07.Stack and Queues/3. Monotonic Stack and Queue/05. Sum of subarray minimum.cpp

narrative.title: The Pipeline Bottleneck Ledger
narrative.scenario: A data pipeline processes every contiguous chunk of a job queue, and each chunk runs as slow as its least-capacity worker. Operations wants one number: the sum of the bottleneck capacities over all possible chunks. Duplicate capacities are allowed, so identical values in different positions still count as separate chunk configurations.
narrative.inputFormat: An integer array arr of worker capacities.
narrative.outputFormat: Return the sum of min(b) over every contiguous subarray b of arr, modulo 10^9 + 7.

testCases.explanation: Single elements sum to 3+1+2+4=10; larger chunks add 1+1+2+1+2+1=7 more.
Each element contributes its value times the count of chunks where it is the minimum.

starterCode.python:
MOD = 10**9 + 7

def sum_subarray_mins(arr):
    n = len(arr)
    prev = [-1] * n   # index of previous strictly smaller element
    next_ = [n] * n   # index of next smaller-or-equal element
    stack = []
    for i in range(n):
        while stack and arr[stack[-1]] > arr[i]:
            stack.pop()
        prev[i] = stack[-1] if stack else -1
        stack.append(i)
    stack = []
    for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
        while stack and arr[stack[-1]] >= arr[i]:
            stack.pop()
        next_[i] = stack[-1] if stack else n
        stack.append(i)
    total = 0
    for i in range(n):
        total = (total + (i - prev[i]) * (next_[i] - i) * arr[i]) % MOD
    return total % MOD

hintLevels: Level 1: Enumerating all n(n+1)/2 subarrays is quadratic — flip the question to per-element contribution.
Level 2: Element arr[i] is the minimum of (i - prevSmaller) * (nextSmaller - i) subarrays.
Level 3: Break ties asymmetrically (strict on one side, non-strict on the other) so duplicates are never double-counted.
